title: Guided Conditional Diffusion for Controllable Traffic Simulation

control_signal.value: Driving rules written in signal temporal logic (speed limit, target speed, no collision, no off-road, goal waypoint, stop sign), alone or combined, specified at test time.

control_mechanism.value: Gradient of differentiable STL robustness perturbs the denoised mean at each sampling step; several guided samples are filtered by rule satisfaction; guidance runs jointly over all agents for interaction rules.

base_model.value: Conditional agent-centric diffusion with 1D-conv U-Net, ResNet encoder on rasterized map and history, unicycle dynamics enforced in the state space, K = 100 steps.

datasets.value: nuScenes; models trained on the train split, evaluated on 100 randomly sampled validation scenes; vehicles only.

metrics.value: Rule-violation metric per rule, realism deviation (Wasserstein distance on longitudinal and lateral acceleration and jerk), failure rate (collision or road departure).

controllability_evidence.value: Speed-limit rule: CTG rule violation 0.019 vs 0.038 for SimNet+opt and 0.033 for BITS+opt, with lower realism deviation (0.359) and failure rate (0.165) than the optimization baselines. Ablation: no guidance gives 1.3802 violation.

stated_limitations.value: Only vehicles are modeled; cyclists and pedestrians deferred to future work.

notes: No dedicated limitations section in packet.
